prompt: What is the condition attached to a Spot VM?
hint: The reason it is cheaper.

choices.text: It runs on older hardware than standard machines
choices.why: Same types, same hardware.

choices.text: It is stopped every night between midnight and six
choices.why: There is no schedule; it is taken back when needed.

choices.text: Google takes it back when it needs it
choices.why: Right. With about thirty seconds' notice.

choices.text: It cannot have a persistent disk
choices.why: Spot machines have ordinary disks.

prompt: n4-standard-2 is 0.0907 USD an hour on demand and 0.053652 on Spot. What is the discount, in per cent, to one decimal?
hint: 1 minus Spot over on demand.

prompt: How does a Spot machine differ from a preemptible one?
hint: One of them has a clock.

choices.text: A preemptible one is also stopped after 24 hours
choices.why: Right. Spot has no such limit.

choices.text: Spot machines cannot be preempted
choices.why: Both can be taken back.

choices.text: Preemptible machines are cheaper and Spot ones dearer
choices.why: Both get Spot prices today.

choices.text: Spot is for GPUs only
choices.why: Any type may be Spot.

prompt: A budget assumes c4a-standard-2 on Spot at 0.044388 USD an hour for the next two years. What is wrong with it?
hint: Which prices does Google revise?

choices.text: Spot prices only apply in Iowa
choices.why: Spot exists in every region, at its own prices.

choices.text: C4A cannot run on Spot
choices.why: The sheet lists its Spot price.

choices.text: Spot prices rise by law after one year
choices.why: No such rule exists.

choices.text: Spot prices move
choices.why: Right. The sum has to be redone, not remembered.

prompt: How does a preemption arrive inside the machine?
hint: A power button.

choices.text: As an email to the project owner
choices.why: Nothing in the machine reads email.

choices.text: As an ACPI soft power-off
choices.why: Right. The operating system starts an orderly shutdown.

choices.text: As a sudden loss of power with no warning
choices.why: There is a warning: about thirty seconds.

choices.text: As a kernel panic
choices.why: It is an orderly signal, not a crash.

prompt: A shutdown script uploads a 3 GiB file before the machine goes. What is the risk?
hint: How long is the window?

choices.text: Shutdown scripts may not use the network
choices.why: They can; the time is the problem.

choices.text: None: Compute Engine waits until the script finishes
choices.why: It waits about thirty seconds, then stops the machine.

choices.text: It is stopped after about thirty seconds anyway
choices.why: Right. Flush a buffer there, do not move a gigabyte.

choices.text: The upload is billed at the Spot price
choices.why: Price is not the risk.

prompt: In the lab, docker stop on the worker with a handler took about two seconds, and on the one without took a tenth of a second. Why?
hint: What did each program do when SIGTERM arrived?

choices.text: One saved a checkpoint; one died at once
choices.why: Right. Exit code 143 is death by SIGTERM.

choices.text: The second container was smaller
choices.why: Both came from the same image.

choices.text: docker stop waits less for --init containers
choices.why: It waits up to 30 seconds for either.

choices.text: The first was still downloading its image
choices.why: The image was built before either ran.

prompt: A process killed by SIGTERM, signal 15, exits with code 128 plus the signal number. What code is that?
A program can tell a preemption from an ordinary shutdown by reading instance/___ on the metadata server, which turns TRUE.
hint: The past participle of the word for taking back.

prompt: Which termination action suits Spot machines inside a managed group?
hint: The group makes a new machine anyway.

choices.text: STOP, so the machine can be started again
choices.why: A stopped machine in a group only holds a disk and a name.

choices.text: RESTART, so the group keeps its size
choices.why: There is no RESTART action.

choices.text: None: groups ignore the action
choices.why: The template's action applies to every machine.

choices.text: DELETE
choices.why: Right. The group recreates from the template.

prompt: Why must a Spot machine have automatic_restart = false?
hint: Can Google promise both?

choices.text: Terraform refuses the plan otherwise
choices.why: The plan accepted true; the API refuses it.

choices.text: Google cannot promise both
choices.why: Right. Compute Engine refuses it at creation.

choices.text: Restarting is billed at the on-demand price
choices.why: The reason is a contradiction, not a price.

choices.text: Spot machines have no boot disk to restart from
choices.why: They have ordinary boot disks.

prompt: max_run_duration is 14,400 seconds. How many hours is that?
hint: 3,600 seconds an hour.

prompt: A batch machine with max_run_duration of four hours is stopped by a preemption after three, and restarted an hour later. When does the time limit end it?
hint: When does the clock start, by gcloud's help?

choices.text: One hour after the restart, completing the four
choices.why: The clock restarts; it does not continue.

choices.text: Immediately, since four hours have passed since creation
choices.why: It counts from the last time the machine entered RUNNING.

choices.text: Four hours after the restart
choices.why: Right. It is measured from the last start.

choices.text: Never, since a preemption cancels the limit
choices.why: The limit is redefined at each run, not cancelled.

prompt: A Spot machine with a local SSD is preempted with the action STOP. What survives?
hint: Which storage belongs to the host?

choices.text: The persistent disks, not the local SSD
choices.why: Right. Lesson 3: a machine that leaves its host loses its local SSD.

choices.text: Everything, since STOP keeps the machine
choices.why: The local SSD stays with the host it left.

choices.text: Only the local SSD
choices.why: The other way round.

choices.text: Nothing, since a preemption deletes every disk
choices.why: STOP keeps the persistent disks.

prompt: What does a managed group do when one of its Spot machines is preempted?
hint: It defends a number.

choices.text: Shrinks its target by one
choices.why: The target stays.

choices.text: Replaces it with a standard machine
choices.why: The template says Spot, so the new one is Spot.

choices.text: Stops every other machine to stay even
choices.why: Nothing else is touched.

choices.text: Recreates it when capacity allows
choices.why: Right. It may wait if there is no room.

prompt: Why can a Spot group sit below its target for hours?
hint: What is short when a preemption happens?

choices.text: Groups only recreate machines once a day
choices.why: They try as soon as they can.

choices.text: There is no capacity to make new ones
choices.why: Right. The group waits for room.

choices.text: The template expires after a preemption
choices.why: Templates do not expire.

choices.text: Spot groups have no autohealing
choices.why: Autohealing is not the issue; capacity is.

prompt: distribution_policy_target_shape = "___" lets a regional Spot group put machines wherever there is room.
hint: Three capital letters.

prompt: The shop wants its web service on Spot to save money. What arrangement does the lesson recommend?
hint: What happens if every machine goes at once?

choices.text: One group of Spot machines with a larger target
choices.why: A capacity shortage takes all of them together.

choices.text: One group whose template mixes Spot and standard machines
choices.why: A template has one provisioning model.

choices.text: A standard base, and Spot for the extra
choices.why: Right. The base answers on its own if Spot disappears.

choices.text: Spot machines with automatic_restart = true
choices.why: Compute Engine refuses that combination.

prompt: Match each workload to whether it belongs on Spot.
hint: What does a preemption cost each one?

pairs.right: Yes: a lost piece is redone
No: it holds the only copy

pairs.left: A twelve-hour job with no checkpoint

prompt: What question does the lesson ask before moving a workload to Spot?
hint: Not whether it runs.

choices.text: What happens if a machine disappears now, mid-work
choices.why: Right. If nobody needs to act, it belongs there.

choices.text: Whether it runs on the E2 series
choices.why: Any series may be Spot.

choices.text: Whether it uses more than 40% CPU
choices.why: Load is not the question.

choices.text: Whether its region has a Spot discount above 50%
choices.why: The discount is the reward, not the test.

prompt: A nightly report takes six hours and cannot save progress. It is moved to Spot and preempted at hour five twice a week. What happened to the saving?
hint: Each preemption costs the hours already run.

choices.text: It doubled, since preempted hours are free
choices.why: Hours run before a preemption are billed.

choices.text: Nothing changed, since the discount applies to every hour
choices.why: The wasted hours are paid too, and the report is late.

choices.text: It was refunded by Google for each preemption
choices.why: There is no refund for preemption.

choices.text: Much of it went on hours redone, and the report is late
choices.why: Right. A long task with no checkpoint is a bad tenant.

prompt: Put the events of a preemption in order.
hint: Notice, shutdown, stop, action.
items: Compute Engine sends an ACPI soft power-off
Services receive SIGTERM and the shutdown script runs
About thirty seconds later the machine is stopped regardless
The termination action, STOP or DELETE, is applied
trap: The termination action decides what is left; it comes after the stop, not before.

prompt: Four e2-standard-2 machines run all month (730 hours) on Spot at 0.040212 USD an hour instead of 0.06701142 on demand. What is saved, in USD, to the cent?
hint: The hourly difference, times 730, times four.

prompt: Which of these did the lab really show? Choose all that apply.
hint: A signal from Docker, a plan from Terraform.

choices.text: A program using SIGTERM to save its work
choices.why: Right; docker stop sent the same signal.

choices.text: A Spot machine being preempted
choices.why: No preemption can be produced from a laptop.

choices.text: The scheduling block Compute Engine would receive
choices.why: Right; the plan showed it.

choices.text: How long a Spot machine runs before preemption
choices.why: Nobody publishes that, and the lab cannot measure it.

prompt: A queue worker on Spot acknowledges each message before processing it. What goes wrong at a preemption?
hint: When is a message delivered again?

choices.text: Nothing: the queue keeps every message forever
choices.why: An acknowledged message is gone from the queue.

choices.text: The message in progress is lost
choices.why: Right. Acknowledge after the work is done, so it is redelivered.

choices.text: The message is processed twice
choices.why: That is the risk of acknowledging after, not before.

choices.text: The worker is moved to a standard machine
choices.why: Nothing moves it.
